svg.text: A243 -- the reach-summary root: the closed-form leaves are curves in the type-F plane, not cell kills; a summary cell's fibre keeps its cores only when it is a pose box
(A) the type-F summary plane (theta, delta)
shaded: TILT-MIN's domain sin theta <= delta < 1 (A237) -- where a
flat-meeter crowd lives; curves: REACH R = s - 2 (contact), LEVER
LEVER (theta >= 57.07)
theta (deg): the partner's tilt; delta: the flat meeter's offset
Below a REACH curve two mode-(a) crowds do not span the wall in contact
(the gap < 1: a third member juts); on the LEVER curve the partner balances
under wall + corner + top-vertex contacts, and R > 2 there: side > 4.017.
Neither is a cell kill (notes/reach243.md s.3): the first needs the holder
on the wall, the second a fixed contact structure.
(B) a survivor crowd and its off-wall holder
the window crowd (theta = 20, delta = 0.362; below every REACH curve at
s-hat) with C holding A toward the corner, force (-1.00, -0.09), floating
A
B
C
C's lowest vertex is at v = 0.75: Lemma HOLD's along-wall holder is not a
wall member, and CHAIN's path from C to a far wall need not run along the
floor -- so 'reaches + bridges must span the wall' has no proof (R1).
(C) one summary cell's FIBRE (h = 0.05) and its cores
200 sampled crowds with the same summary to within h; the two role
cores (dark) = intersections of bodies: areas 0.84 / 0.89
The core is what the no-room leaf may subtract (A172's K', A242 s.2). This
cell is the window crowd's: its fibre is THIN and the cores stay large. A
GENERIC cell's fibre is fat: every occupied bin at h = 0.2 has an EMPTY
core (results/reach243.md s.5) -- R3 reads nothing until the cell is a pose box.

Sources: A239 rings_below_4.md s.1, s.3 (REACH, LEVER); A237 pocket_waste.md s.1 (TILT-MIN); A218 k0_count.md s.3 (HOLD); A233 local_lock.md s.3 (RADIAL, CHAIN); A242 crowd242.md s.2 (cores); results/reach243.jsonl.
